messages:
maria: heads-up: nightly RAG eval (prod-cohort) shows a sharp rank-shift for a subset of queries, recall@10 down ~3.5% vs yesterday
vikram: link to the report?
maria: https://internal.reports/nightly/rag/1865432099 - top summary at the top, full CSV attached
eval-bot: nightly run complete: dataset=prod-cohort, model=reranker-v2.3, embed-model=instructor-large-quant, recall@10=0.807, prev=0.842, delta=-0.035
kevin: I deployed reranker-v2.3 yesterday morning (02:10 UTC) with lightweight tuning for diversity. No infra changes. cc @vikram
vikram: can we check embed drift first? recall drop could be from embeddings shifting index order
sophie: running a quick embed-sim diff on a 5k sample now. will paste numbers shortly
ollie: I'll verify index build artifacts - maybe a stale shard or different tokenizer used during offline indexing
kevin: fwiw the reranker change was small (added pairwise loss weight 0.1). I didn't touch encoder weights, we use frozen embed vector from instructor-large-quant.
sophie: quick numbers: mean cosine similarity between todays and yesterdays embeddings on sample = 0.9981, median=0.9992. outliers ~0.7% with drop <0.9
maria: so embeddings mostly stable. can we get per-query rank movement histogram?
eval-bot: attached: rank_shift_histogram.png and topk_deltas.csv (small note: many queries moved from rank1-3 to 4-8)
vikram: that pattern looks like reranker scoring reshuffle rather than recall loss from retriever. Does reranker v2.3 change score scaling?
kevin: yes, pairwise objective changed scores magnitude slightly, but we apply a soft rescale in postprocess. maybe bug there
ollie: found one suspicious artifact during index validation: index-metadata.json built yesterday references tokenizer_version=2024-11-02 while pipeline used 2024-10-29. Hash mismatch: index_hash=ab12... vs expected ab13...
sophie: hmm embeddings were stable, but if index tokenization changed, that could change doc chunking and retrieval candidates
maria: timeline: 00:50 UTC nightly index build (tokenizer 2024-11-02), 02:10 UTC reranker rollout v2.3, 03:00 UTC eval run. Which change is causal?
vikram: hypothesis A: index tokenizer mismatch changed doc chunk boundaries -> different topk candidates -> reranker reshuffle amplifies rank changes. Hypothesis B: reranker scoring scale bug causes demotion of heads.
kevin: I can quickly run ablation: score old reranker model (v2.2) on today's candidate sets to see if recall recovers
ollie: and I can rebuild index with the previous tokenizer (2024-10-29) onto a temp table and re-run retrieval to compare candidate overlap
sophie: running ablation: using today's candidates, rerank with v2.2 -> recall@10=0.841 (close to yesterday). running with v2.3 -> 0.808 (matches nightly).
maria: that strongly implicates reranker change. good catch Sophie.
vikram: but why would reranker behave differently only when index tokenizer changed? or is it independent?
sophie: I checked pairwise score distributions: v2.3 scores have heavier tails; when candidate set has more near-duplicate chunks (due to boundary shifts), pairwise objective tends to over-penalize certain passages -> demotes correct doc sometimes
kevin: actionable: revert v2.3 rollout to canary only, push v2.2 back to prod, and then run full nightly. I'll schedule rollback now.
ollie: I'll also start a clean index rebuild on staging with tokenizer 2024-11-02 to ensure parity and run end-to-end tests
maria: adding test: generate candidates for 1k queries and compute candidate overlap Jaccard between index versions. if overlap < 0.95 we block reranker rollouts until we pin tokenizers
vikram: also add a unit test to the reranker pipeline that checks that score rescaling is applied consistently regardless of candidate distribution
kevin: rollback scheduled for 1865432330 UTC. ping once done and I'll re-run eval
sophie: logged reproducer + ablation results in the ticket: ML-4521. attaching minimal script: ```python
# reproduce rerank ablation
candidates = load_candidates('today_candidates.json')
for q in sample_queries:
    s_old = rerank('v2.2', candidates[q])
    s_new = rerank('v2.3', candidates[q])
    compare_recall(s_old, s_new)
```
maria: thanks everyone. quick postmortem draft: root cause = reranker v2.3 scoring behavior interacting with small index tokenization drift -> amplified rank shifts; mitigation = rollback + tighter compatibility checks between indexer tokenizers and reranker assumptions
eval-bot: follow-ups created: ML-4521 (ablation), INF-998 (indexizer parity job), ML-4522 (reranker unit test)
vikram: can someone own the postmortem? I'll start the doc, @maria can you add the timeline and numbers?
maria: yep I'll take timeline + summary
kevin: I'll own rollout gating (add canary verifications and score-distribution checks)
ollie: I'll own index parity infra job
sophie: I'll expand ablation and add a small regression test in nightly eval harness
maria: closing for now, will update thread when rollback and re-eval finish :thumbsup:
eval-bot: rollback finished at 1865432330, reranker reverted to v2.2, re-run queued
maria: re-eval results incoming...
